**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/25 (Thu) 22:39
- [USER] User inquired about regions within Queensland that are prone to extreme weather events like cyclones or storms.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] North Queensland is highly susceptible to severe tropical cyclones between November and April each year; Cyclone Yasi in 2011 caused massive damage.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Far North Queensland experiences heavy rainfall and flooding during the wet season, which lasts from November to April; the worst flood in recent years was in 2019.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Southeast Queensland is prone to severe thunderstorms, strong winds, hail, and heavy rainfall; tornadoes have affected the area, including one in Burrum Heads in 2013.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Central Queensland has experienced severe droughts, bushfires, cyclones, and flooding.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Queensland is one of the most disaster-prone states in Australia, and awareness of risks is important for residents and visitors.
- [USER] User expressed surprise at Queensland's susceptibility to extreme weather events and asked about preparation and safety measures during disasters.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] People can prepare and stay safe during extreme weather events by staying informed, having an emergency kit, protecting their home, planning for evacuation, staying indoors during events, and keeping their phone charged.
- [USER] User asked about organizations in Queensland that provide assistance during and after disasters.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Queensland State Emergency Service (SES) manages disaster response and recovery efforts.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Australian Red Cross provides support, emergency relief, shelter, and emotional support to affected individuals.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] St. John Ambulance Australia offers first aid services during emergencies.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Disaster Recovery Australia helps communities recover from natural disasters with counseling, financial assistance, and practical support.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Salvation Army provides emergency relief, food, and shelter to disaster-affected individuals.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lifeline offers crisis support and suicide prevention services during and after disasters.
- [USER] User inquired about what to do if unable to evacuate during a disaster.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] If unable to evacuate, individuals should seek shelter in a secure part of their home, stock up on supplies, stay informed, have a communication plan, and stay calm.
- [USER] User asked if it's possible for people in high-risk areas to fully protect themselves from natural disasters.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] It is not always possible to fully protect against natural disasters; preparations can minimize damage but cannot eliminate risks.
